architecture.mechanism: Global mean surface temperature will continue to rise regardless of mitigation efforts, making ambient heat-rejection increasingly difficult for any outdoor enclosure in warming climates.
architecture.intervention: Replace fixed-passive designs (which assume a stable climate baseline) with a climate-adaptive passive cabinet: high-albedo exterior coating combined with a phase-change material (PCM) thermal buffer sized for the projected elevated ambient temperature distribution, plus a chimney-effect ventilation stack sized to the new temperature differential.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced probability of internal temperature exceeding 55 degrees Celsius during the 95th-percentile operational hour, because heat gain is temporarily absorbed by the PCM and then rejected via the stack during cooler overnight windows, even as outdoor ambient baselines shift upward.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument two prototype cabinets (one with PCM + stack, one reference with only paint) at an Indian summer field site over one full season; the null hypothesis (PCM stack confers no benefit) is rejected if the treated cabinet's internal temperature stays below 55 degrees Celsius for at least 95 percent of hours while the reference does not, with a per-cabinet incremental cost below 400 dollars.
